source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Why does the lecture suggest the AGI (artificial general intelligence) milestone passed quietly, without much public agreement that it had happened?

options.text: The definition of AGI itself shifts each time a capability threshold is reached.
options.feedback: This is the moving-goalposts problem: the bar keeps being redrawn as models improve, so clearing the original bar never registered as a single, agreed-upon event.

options.text: The companies that build these models suppress announcements about AGI.
options.feedback: The notes describe no concealment. The explanation offered is about the definition moving over time, not about anyone hiding a result.

options.text: No model has reached average human performance on ordinary tasks.
options.feedback: This contradicts the argument in the notes, which was that average-human performance across most tasks had in fact been reached under the older definition.

options.text: AGI was redefined as a legal term with no technical meaning.
options.feedback: The shifting described in the notes happens in how the field informally talks about capability thresholds, not in law or regulation.
